requirement:
The Markdown outline MUST expose each prose paragraph as an anonymous
`paragraph` node under its nearest enclosing outline container, including
paragraphs before the first heading and inside list items, quotations, and
Markdown directive bodies. Paragraphs MUST use the shared anonymous-selector
rules under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Heading text
and literal code-block contents MUST NOT create paragraph nodes.
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.paragraphs` has no {test} references or :test: anchors. The `references` tool shows no sites for it. A search of `crates` for a `paragraph` node kind or a `paragraph@` selector found nothing. The book (`md/requirements/sdk/sources/markdown.md`, "Markdown outline definition") says the Markdown outline currently covers sections only. It says the paragraph and block contracts "are not yet implemented".

Nothing tests these obligations:
- Each prose paragraph is exposed as an anonymous `paragraph` node.
- Paragraphs sit under their nearest enclosing container. That includes paragraphs before the first heading and inside list items, quotations and directive bodies.
- Paragraph selectors follow the shared anonymous-selector rules (`kind@hash`, with `#N` disambiguation of otherwise identical siblings).
- Heading text creates no paragraph node.
- Literal code-block contents create no paragraph node.

The paragraph-related tests in `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/tests.rs` cover structural-hash behaviour and comment classification. They do not check paragraph node exposure. No {fixme} acknowledges the gap.

text: The Markdown outline MUST expose each prose paragraph as an anonymous
`paragraph` node under its nearest enclosing outline container, including
paragraphs before the first heading and inside list items, quotations, and
Markdown directive bodies. Paragraphs MUST use the shared anonymous-selector
and literal code-block contents MUST NOT create paragraph nodes.
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
